research_question: What is the canonical, evidence-based taxonomy of UI/UX and web-conversion design principles — a clustered set of ~12-18 self-contained, teachable topics — that comprehensively covers product UI craft, visual and interaction design, accessibility, and landing-page conversion, where each topic carries a stable slug, scope, depth tier, 3-5 authoritative grounding sources, and yields agent-checkable rules that collectively cover the design-quality gauntlet's six axes (design-tokens, component-usage, visual-hierarchy, mobile-responsive, accessibility, design-handoff) and visual-review's seven categories (color, layout, typography, copy, a11y, console-error, regression)?

phases.name: Landscape
phases.objective: Survey the canonical principle taxonomies that already exist and map their overlapping categories: Nielsen Norman 10 usability heuristics, Laws of UX, Gestalt principles, Refactoring UI chapters, WCAG 2.2 POUR, Material 3 / Apple HIG principle sets, and Baymard/CXL conversion frameworks.
sub_questions: What are the established UI/UX and conversion principle taxonomies, and how does each cluster its principles?
Which principle categories recur across three or more authoritative sources (the high-consensus core)?
phases.evidence_priorities: Primary authoritative sources only: nngroup.com (10 heuristics + topic taxonomy), lawsofux.com, refactoringui.com (book TOC), w3.org WCAG 2.2 (POUR + SC categories), m3.material.io and developer.apple.com HIG (as principle sources, not product plugs), baymard.com (UX research catalog), cxl.com (conversion research).
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 5+ canonical taxonomies are surveyed and a cross-source category-overlap map is produced.

phases.name: Mechanics
phases.objective: Determine the right granularity and clustering for a ~12-18 topic teachable taxonomy — which principles deserve a standalone guide, which fold together, and what cluster structure (Foundations / Visual / Interaction / Accessibility / Conversion / Systems) best organizes them.
sub_questions: At what granularity should principles be split into teachable guides (e.g., is typography one topic or three; do color and contrast separate)?
How do app/product UI principles and landing-page conversion principles cluster — shared foundations vs domain-specific topics?
phases.evidence_priorities: Tables of contents of authoritative books (Refactoring UI, Don't Make Me Think, The Design of Everyday Things, Universal Principles of Design), design-system documentation structures (Material, Polaris, Carbon), and design-curriculum syllabi from IxDF / NN/g.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when a clustered ~12-18 topic taxonomy is justified against the structure of 3+ source taxonomies/curricula.

phases.name: Failure Modes
phases.objective: Identify the most common, checkable design failures each candidate principle prevents, so every topic yields agent-applicable rules mirroring what visual-review and design-quality actually catch.
sub_questions: What are the most common UI/UX and conversion design mistakes, and which principle does each map to?
Which failures are mechanically checkable (contrast ratio, tap-target size, token usage, heading order) versus judgment calls (hierarchy, cohort fit)?
phases.evidence_priorities: NN/g mistake/guideline lists, Baymard checkout and UX failure studies, WCAG failure techniques and audit checklists (WebAIM), conversion-leak catalogs (CXL), and common front-end rendering defects (console errors, FOUC, layout shift).
phases.stop_condition: Complete when each candidate topic has 2+ concrete checkable failure modes attached.

phases.name: Contrarian
phases.objective: Challenge the taxonomy: where authorities disagree, and what a pure heuristic list omits (motion/animation, content/copy/UX writing, performance-as-UX, internationalization, ethics/dark patterns) — and whether those deserve standalone topics.
sub_questions: What important principle areas do the standard heuristic lists omit, and should each be a separate teachable topic or folded into an existing one?
phases.evidence_priorities: Critiques of Nielsen's heuristics, the aesthetic-usability debate, modern additions (Core Web Vitals as UX, content design / UX writing as a discipline, dark-pattern / deceptive-design taxonomies, motion and reduced-motion).
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ substantive gaps or disagreements in the standard taxonomies are documented with evidence.

search_strategy: Laws of UX complete list Jon Yablonski
Refactoring UI table of contents chapters
WCAG 2.2 POUR principles success criteria categories
Gestalt principles of visual perception UI design
CXL conversion optimization principles landing page
Apple Human Interface Guidelines principles foundations
visual hierarchy typography contrast spacing design principles
exclusion_criteria: Non-authoritative listicle blogs without primary sourcing
Product marketing pages presented as principle sources
Pre-2015 material superseded by WCAG 2.2 / Material 3 / modern conversion research

sections: Recommended Taxonomy (12-18 topics, clustered, with slug + scope + sources)
required_output_schema.per_finding_format: Each finding: claim, supporting evidence, confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), source URLs, counter-evidence if any
required_output_schema.per_source_format: Each source: URL, title, credibility (1-5), recency, type (primary/secondary/opinion)

openai_instructions: Construct a MECE ~12-18 topic taxonomy of UI/UX + conversion design principles. For EACH topic give: a stable UPPER_SNAKE slug, a one-line scope, its cluster, and 2-3 concrete checkable rules it yields. Then map the full topic set to these review axes and explicitly confirm coverage: design-quality (design-tokens, component-usage, visual-hierarchy, mobile-responsive, accessibility, design-handoff) and visual-review (color, layout, typography, copy, a11y, console-error, regression). Flag any axis not covered by at least one topic.
gemini_instructions: Pull and compare the canonical principle sources (NN/g 10 heuristics, Laws of UX full list, Refactoring UI TOC, WCAG 2.2 POUR + SC categories, Gestalt principles, Baymard/CXL conversion catalogs). Extract the recurring principle CATEGORIES across them and cite a real URL for each. Produce a comparison table showing which categories appear in which source, to reveal the high-consensus core vs source-specific additions.
claude_instructions: Verify the authority and recency of each cited source, reconcile overlapping/duplicate categories across taxonomies into a single deduplicated topic list, and investigate the contrarian angle: what is missing from heuristic lists (motion, content design/UX writing, performance UX, ethics/dark patterns, internationalization) and whether each deserves its own teachable topic or folds into an existing one.
